# 2 Maccabees Chapter 8 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 2 Maccabees 8 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/2MA_008_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Judas Maccabeus and his companions began moving through the villages secretly, rallying family members and recruiting any who had held onto their Jewish faith. Within a short time they had gathered about six thousand men.

**2** They prayed to the LORD: look at your people, crushed on every side. Have compassion on the temple, desecrated by godless men.

**3** Have mercy on the city, half in ruins, on the verge of being wiped from the earth. Hear the blood that cries out to you.

**4** Remember the massacre of innocent children. Remember the blasphemies against your name. And show — in the open — how much you hate evil.

**5** The moment Maccabeus had his force organized, the Gentiles found him impossible to stop, because the LORD's wrath had given way to mercy.

**6** He would fall on towns and villages by surprise, putting them to the torch, retaking key positions, routing enemy forces again and again.

**7** He favored night operations above everything. His courage became the talk of the region.

**8** Philip could see it clearly: this man was growing stronger with each passing week. The attacks were becoming more frequent, the victories more decisive. Philip wrote to Ptolemy, governor of Coelesyria and Phoenicia, demanding reinforcements.

**9** Ptolemy acted at once. He sent Nicanor son of Patroclus — one of the king's top officials — at the head of a mixed force of at least twenty thousand soldiers from various nations, with orders to eliminate the entire Jewish population of Judea. He also sent along Gorgias, an experienced field commander.

**10** Nicanor had a plan: he would cover the two-thousand-talent tribute owed to Rome by selling the Jews he captured as slaves.

**11** He immediately sent notices to the coastal cities, advertising a slave sale and promising ninety Jewish slaves per talent. He had no idea what was about to fall on him from the Almighty.

**12** When Judas got word of Nicanor's advance, he told his men the army was coming.

**13** The ones who panicked — those whose faith in God's justice had crumbled — slipped away and disappeared.

**14** The rest sold off whatever they had left and together they prayed to the LORD: rescue those whom this godless Nicanor has already presold as slaves before a single battle has been fought.

**15** Not for our own sake if it must be so — but for the sake of the covenants you made with our fathers, and because you called us by your own holy and glorious name.

**16** Maccabeus assembled his six thousand men and spoke to them directly: don't let the enemy intimidate you. Don't let the numbers frighten you. These Gentiles have no right to be attacking us. Fight well.

**17** Keep what they did in front of your eyes — the desecration of the holy place, the humiliation of the city, the destruction of everything our ancestors passed down to us.

**18** "They put their trust in weapons and in nerve," he said. "We put our trust in the almighty God, who with a single nod can bring down every one of those men advancing on us — and the whole world besides."

**19** He reminded them of how God had rescued their ancestors before. In the days of Sennacherib, one hundred and eighty-five thousand men had been destroyed overnight.

**20** And in the battle with the Galatians in Babylonia: eight thousand Jews had fought alongside four thousand Macedonians. When the Macedonians were in trouble, those eight thousand destroyed one hundred and twenty thousand — because help came down from heaven. And they came away with enormous plunder.

**21** By the time he finished, his men were filled with courage. They were ready to die for the law and for their country. He divided the force into four companies.

**22** He placed his brothers Simon, Joseph, and Jonathan over three of them, with fifteen hundred men each.

**23** He appointed Eleazar to read publicly from the holy scriptures. His watchword was: "God's help." Then he led the first company himself and charged at Nicanor's lines.

**24** With the Almighty fighting beside them, they cut down more than nine thousand of the enemy. They wounded and incapacitated most of Nicanor's army. They drove all of them to flight.

**25** They took the money from the people who had come to buy Jewish slaves. They chased the fleeing enemy until they had to stop — the hour was too late to continue.

**26** The sabbath was the next day, and out of reverence for it they broke off the pursuit.

**27** They gathered the enemy's weapons and stripped the bodies of their spoils. Then they kept the sabbath — with abundant praise and thanks to the LORD who had preserved them that day and shown them his mercy at last.

**28** After the sabbath, they divided the spoils. Part went to those who had been tortured under the persecution, to the widows, and to the orphans. The rest was shared among the fighters and their families.

**29** When the distribution was complete, they gathered for prayer — all of them — begging the merciful LORD to be fully and finally reconciled to his servants.

**30** In subsequent fighting against the forces of Timothy and Bacchides, they killed over twenty thousand. They took control of several commanding hillforts. They distributed an enormous quantity of plunder — equal shares for those who had suffered torture, for the orphans, for the widows, for the elderly.

**31** They gathered and stored the enemy's weapons in secure positions, then brought the rest of the spoils back to Jerusalem.

**32** They killed the commander of Timothy's army — a thoroughly evil man who had done enormous damage to the Jews.

**33** Back in Jerusalem, celebrating their victory, they tracked down Callisthenes and others who had burned the sacred gates. These men had taken shelter in a small house. The fighters burned them in it. They got what their wickedness deserved.

**34** Nicanor — the wretch three times cursed — who had brought a thousand slave-dealers to purchase the Jewish people,

**35** was utterly humiliated by the very men he had planned to sell. With the LORD's help, Judas's fighters brought him down. Nicanor stripped off his magnificent uniform and fled alone through the backcountry like a runaway slave, making his way to Antioch. He had accomplished exactly one thing: destroying his own army.

**36** The man who had promised to pay Rome's tribute by selling the people of Jerusalem ended up telling everyone the opposite story: the Jews have a protector. Following God's laws makes them untouchable.
